name: Abyssinia Poker
description: Abyssinia is a five-card stud, high-low poker variant where players 'buy' cards from a central market. It introduces financial resource management to traditional poker mechanics.

overview.description: Abyssinia is a five-card stud, high-low poker variant where players 'buy' cards from a central market. It introduces financial resource management to traditional poker mechanics.

history.origins: Originating in the United States, Abyssinia was once a staple of 'Dealer's Choice' home games. It was extensively documented in Scarne on Cards (1949).
timeline: 1940s: Emerged as a competitive stud variant in high-stakes home games.
1950s: Standard tier-pricing (2u/1u/4u) for ranks became the house standard.
Present: Remained a niche favorite in professional poker circles.
history.cultural: Reflects the American post-war home-game culture of introducing complex rules to standard gambling games.
history.evolution: Replaced the random deal of Five-Card Stud with a tiered-cost economy for specific card ranks.

setup.dealing: 1. All players ante. 2. Dealer turns up two cards and places them beside the face-down deck (the Market). 3. No initial cards to players; each builds a 5-card hand over 5 buy rounds.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips, and a dealer button.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest or lowest hand (or both) at the showdown.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Ante**: All players post the ante. 2. **Market Setup**: Dealer turns up two cards and places them beside the deck. 3. **Buy Phase**: Starting left of dealer, each player buys one card from the market (face-up) or stock (top card, revealed on purchase). 4. **Refill**: Purchased market cards are replaced immediately from the stock. 5. **Bet Phase**: After each buy round, a standard betting round. 6. **Repetition**: Buy/bet sequence repeats 5 times until each player has 5 cards. 7. **Declaration**: Active players secret-declare High, Low, or Both using chips in hand. 8. **Showdown**: Cards revealed; pot split per declarations.
keyRules: Market cards cost based on rank: 2-5 (2u), 6-K (1u), Ace (4u).
Cards bought from the stock are revealed to the table immediately.
Market purchases remain face-up if taken from the market row.
Pig Rule: If declaring 'Both', you must win both High and Low halves solo or win nothing.
Each player must buy exactly one card per buy phase (mandatory).

strategy.basic: Keep your 'down' cards a secret while tracking what others buy face-up. Cheap 6-K cards are great for bluffing a high hand.
strategy.intermediate: Aces are versatile but expensive. Only buy them if they complete a flush/straight or a top-tier low.
strategy.advanced: Defensive rank-blocking: If the refill shows a 2 and an opponent is building a low, buy that 2 even if you have a high hand.
tips: Being on the dealer's left is high value; you get the first choice of the fresh market refill.
Check the threshold: Ensure you actually have an 8-low or better before declaring Low.
Track opponent face-up purchases to estimate their declaration direction before chips-in-fist.

variations.name: Fixed Market Price
variations.description: All cards cost 2 units regardless of rank. Removes the tiered economy.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation description is documented but engine-level overrides for market pricing have not yet been encoded.

variations.name: Hidden Stock
variations.description: Cards bought from the stock remain face-down (private), instead of being revealed to the table.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Hidden stock is a presentation and visibility change; specific engine overrides for visibility are not yet modeled.

variations.name: 7-Card Abyssinia
variations.description: Hand size is 7; best 5 of 7 play. Buy phases extend to 5 rounds.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Seven-card version is described in rules text; structured overrides for hand size and buy rounds are not yet specified.

scoring.description: High-Low Split pot. 50% to the best poker hand, 50% to the best low hand (8-or-better qualifier).
scoring.winCondition: Highest poker rank wins the high half of the pot; lowest qualifying hand (8-high or better) wins the low half.

synthesis.shortDescription: A professional 5-card stud variant where players buy their ranks from a fixed-cost market, followed by high-low splits.

hero.title: ABYSSINIA
hero.subtitle: Market-Driven High-Low Poker
hero.tagline: In this market, victory is bought, not dealt.
